config.owner.conf:
# /etc/usb16x16/dante/owner.conf: how usb16x16-dante.service starts the owner.
# Written by usb16x16-apply 2026-11-17T04:28:31Z; read by usb16x16-dante-start.
METERS=1
config.transport.conf:
# /etc/usb16x16/dante/transport.conf: transport settings for usb16x16-dante-owner,
# read by usb16x16-dante-start (the -transport form) beside owner.conf. Installed
# by install-dante-lowlatency.sh, PRIME_DROP and CAPTURE_DRAIN by install-owner-anchor.sh,
# PRIME_DROP=28 by install-owner-ratepoll.sh, the 96000 keys by install-dante-rate96.sh, their
# prime drop by install-dante-rate96-drop.sh, raised to 96 by install-dante-rate96-drop96.sh,
# the 88200 keys by install-dante-rate882.sh;
# the applier never writes this file.
#
# The return queue's target depth, frames. 144 is the owner's default. At 96 its
# floor measured 45 to 48 frames over five anchors, a battery and a loaded hour
# on 2026-10-12/13 (RESULTS.md, "Both Inferno knobs at 1 ms and the return queue
# at 96").
RX_QUEUE=96
#
# SAMPLE_RATE_DESIGN.md step 4 (2026-10-17): a host at another rate becomes a
# request for the arbiter (usb16x16-dante-rate.path), through the owner's
# --rate-request-file. Needs owner c8b484ac or later.
RATE_REQUESTS=1
#
# The same round trip at every host open (work/mac-driver-spike/SPIKE_PLAN.md,
# Phases B and C, 2026-10-30): the outgoing prime drops a constant number of
# frames of the host's first block, and the gadget capture PCM is restarted at
# each host stop so every session starts empty on a period boundary. Needs owner
# abee374a or later. 28 (was 24) passed the battery on owner c84e6a36 at
# daw_timeline 528 on 2026-10-30; 32 sits on the prime floor (block 48 + packet
# 32 + margin 16 = 96) and skipped a frame on 2 of 12 primes.
PRIME_DROP=28
CAPTURE_DRAIN=1
#
# 96 kHz (RATE96_PLAN.md phase 5, 2026-10-31): every depth doubled from the 48 kHz
# figures, so each lasts the same time (arm A). Clean on the 8-channel loop:
# battery 2026-10-29 (680 / daw_timeline 916, soak and bitexact PASS after a Metric
# Halo reboot) and 0 playback faults in about 205 minutes without a capture on
# 2026-10-31. The prime drop and capture drain at 96 (2026-10-31 evening sweep on owner
# c84e6a36, six opens each, capture drain on): D=48 958 x6, D=72 934-935, D=96 910 x6,
# no unanchored prime; without them the opens drew 919-1004. 48 was installed first
# (958 at every open). 96 passed the battery on 2026-11-01 on a candidate of the same
# owner (911 x4, 600 s soak and bitexact PASS, 0 faults, return queue floor 80): 0.5 ms
# lower. A drop over 48 needs the start wrapper that takes 0 to 96 for a 96 kHz key.
RX_QUEUE_96000=192
RX_SLACK_96000=192
BUFFER_96000=2048
TX_LEAD_96000=256
GUARD_96000=512
USB_PERIOD_96000=96
USB_BUFFER_96000=960
PRIME_DROP_96000=96
CAPTURE_DRAIN_96000=1
#
# 88.2 kHz (RATE882_PLAN.md, 2026-11-01): 96's arm A depths, the same frames (about 9 %
# longer in time). Prime-drop sweep with capture drain on owner c84e6a36, six opens each:
# D=48 912-913, D=72 888-889, D=84 876-877 on 3 opens and 932-933 on 3 (the prime anchored
# a block later), D=96 909-920. 72 is the last drop that anchored early on every open.
# The +-1 is 88.2's non-integer packet grid.
RX_QUEUE_88200=192
RX_SLACK_88200=192
BUFFER_88200=2048
TX_LEAD_88200=256
GUARD_88200=512
USB_PERIOD_88200=96
USB_BUFFER_88200=960
PRIME_DROP_88200=72
CAPTURE_DRAIN_88200=1
config.asound-inferno-owner.conf:
# 2026-11-01, RATE882_PLAN.md phase 2: the installed config
# (asound-inferno-owner-usb-aoip-rate96.conf, 8549af7e at 48 kHz) offering 88200
# beside 44100, 48000 and 96000, the one change. A set from Controller or Dante
# Switcher to 88200 is handed to the arbiter like 44.1 and 96; transport.conf's
# _88200 keys give the owner its depths there. The applier rewrites SAMPLE_RATE
# below; SUPPORTED_SAMPLE_RATES it never writes. Installed by
# service/install-dante-rate882.sh.
#
# 2026-10-31, RATE96_PLAN.md phase 5: the installed config
# (asound-inferno-owner-usb-aoip.conf, 54f3f0ba at 48 kHz) offering 96000 beside
# 44100 and 48000, the one change. 96 passed its battery on the 8-channel loop
# (2026-10-29) and ran about 205 minutes without a playback fault (2026-10-31).
# A set from Controller or Dante Switcher to 96000 is handed to the arbiter like
# 44.1; transport.conf's _96000 keys give the owner its depths there. The applier
# rewrites SAMPLE_RATE below; SUPPORTED_SAMPLE_RATES it never writes. Installed
# by service/install-dante-rate96.sh.
#
# 2026-10-30: the Dante device is named after the project. The installed config
# (asound-inferno-owner-rate44-48-arbiter.conf, 19da7c70 at 48 kHz) with NAME
# "USB-AoIP" in place of "USB-16x16-Inferno", the one change. DEVICE_ID and
# STATE_ID stay, so the Pi's own saved subscriptions (RX 1-16 <- Pulse Output
# 17-32) carry over; the Pulse's subscriptions to the Pi name the device and are
# made again after the install (TX n@USB-AoIP -> Input 16+n). The applier still
# rewrites SAMPLE_RATE below. Installed by service/install-dante-name.sh.
#
# SAMPLE_RATE_DESIGN.md step 7 for 44.1 kHz, 2026-10-28: the installed config
# (asound-inferno-owner-rate48-arbiter.conf, 0a1688e1) offering 44100 beside
# 48000, the one change. 44.1 passed its battery on the real loop on 2026-10-27
# and its start slips were fixed by owner rate5 (2578c73d). A set from
# Controller or Dante Switcher to 44100 is now handed to the arbiter, which
# moves the stack only when the Mac is at that rate ("the Mac decides"); a host
# at 44.1 becomes a request through the owner's --rate-request-file. The
# applier rewrites SAMPLE_RATE below; SUPPORTED_SAMPLE_RATES it never writes.
# Installed by service/install-dante-rate44.sh.
#
# SAMPLE_RATE_DESIGN.md step 4, 2026-10-17, staged: the step-2 config plus
# RATE_REQUEST_FILE (patches/0005): a set from Controller or Dante Switcher to
# an offered rate other than the current one is handed to the arbiter
# (usb16x16-dante-rate.path). With 48000 the only rate offered, nothing is ever
# handed on: a set to 48000 is acknowledged and any other is refused, as before.
#
# Step 2, 2026-10-16: the installed config
# (asound-inferno-owner-both1ms.conf) plus patches/0004's keys, for the
# plugin built from patches 0001-0004. The endpoint publishes its rate
# (48 kHz, the only one offered until a rate change exists) to Dante
# Controller and netaudio and refuses a set to anything else. Board-info
# byte 0x17 = 0x18: sample-rate (0x08) and encoding (0x10) configuration,
# nothing else (netaudio's decoding of the capability word). DEVICE_ID is
# eth0's MAC plus process 0000, which netaudio can read as a MAC; STATE_ID
# keeps the saved subscriptions in the old ID's directory, shared with a
# rollback.
# EXPERIMENT 2026-10-12, not installed: asound-inferno-owner.conf with both latency
# knobs at 1 ms: the Pi's own receive latency (TX_LATENCY_NS in this revision) and the
# figure it advertises to its receivers (RX_LATENCY_NS). RESULTS.md, "Latency
# settings as wired". Run through usb16x16-dante-candidate CONFIG=.
# ALSA config for usb16x16-dante-owner (OWNER_DESIGN.md). The same device identity
# as asound-inferno.conf, so the saved subscriptions and Controller routes apply.
# Used through ALSA_CONFIG_PATH by run-owner.sh with the plugin built from
# patches/0001 (plugins/xrun-option); nothing system-wide is changed.
</usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf>
pcm.inferno {
	type inferno
	NAME "USB-AoIP"
	# netaudio takes its MAC from the mDNS id and cannot decode the ASCII one
	# ("USB16x16"), so it sent no settings queries. eth0's MAC plus process 0000,
	# the form the Ferrofish uses; STATE_ID (patches/0004) keeps the saved
	# subscriptions under the old ID's directory.
	DEVICE_ID "88a29e8b01e40000"
	STATE_ID "5553423136783136"
	BIND_IP "eth0"
	SAMPLE_RATE "48000"
	# patches/0004
	SUPPORTED_SAMPLE_RATES "44100,48000,88200,96000"
	BOARD_FLAGS_17 "18"
	# patches/0005
	RATE_REQUEST_FILE "/run/usb16x16-dante/rate-request"
	RX_CHANNELS "16"
	TX_CHANNELS "16"
	# 24 removes the transmit dither on 24-bit flows
	TX_SOURCE_BIT_DEPTH "24"
	# the two knobs are crossed in this revision; keep them equal. 2 ms is the
	# value the prototype was measured at.
	RX_LATENCY_NS "1000000"
	TX_LATENCY_NS "1000000"
	# patches/0001: a playback underrun is not reported; the owner moves its own
	# pointer. Without this the only way out of an underrun is a six-second prepare.
	XRUN_REPORT "0"
	# The owner does not poll the device: its state is a function of the clock,
	# and with flows up the descriptor fires thousands of times a second.
	DISABLE_POLLFD "1"
}
